title: SLO Oncall Steward Field Kit — Capacity Negotiation & Error-Budget Playbook
author: Ravi Kapoor
body:
Overview

Purpose: This field kit consolidates the SRE oncall steward responsibilities, concrete negotiation patterns for error budgets and capacity, templated communications, and tooling recipes for rapid, evidence-led decisions during SLO pressure periods. It is intended for oncall SREs, service stewards, and product owners who must make runtime tradeoffs with visibility and stakeholder buy-in.

Scope: SLO-driven decision making for Redwood Inference production inference services, including host-facing APIs, dedicated capacity tenants, and private deployments. This playbook covers: detection thresholds, short and medium-term capacity hedges, customer communication templates, incident review inputs, and observability/CLI commands to collect decisive evidence.

Owner & Audience
- Document owner: Ravi Kapoor (eng-sre)
- Primary audience: oncall SREs, service owners, product managers
- Secondary audience: capacity planners, support engineers, solutions engineering

Key principles (why this matters)
1) Evidence-first: every error-budget or capacity negotiation requires a concise evidence packet (quantiles, traffic profile, tenant impact, recent deploys).
2) Minimal customer impact: prefer graceful degradations and token/prioritization lanes over full outages.
3) Short-cycle experiments: prefer short, reversible capacity hedges (30–120 minutes) with automated rollback.
4) Clear escalation: decisions that change customer SLAs or billing require documented approval and an oncall handoff.

Immediate decision checklist (one-page)
1. Confirm SLO breach signal: which SLO (p50/p95/p99/availability/error-rate) and which service surface. Include alert ID and start time.
2. Gather evidence packet (see Evidence Packet template).
3. Estimate headroom: hot-pool and pre-warmed capacity available in next 5/15/60 minutes. Use CLI commands below.
4. Select mitigation pattern: redirect, degrade, throttle, evict, or burst-reserve.
5. Execute mitigation with guardrails and record intent in incident ticket.
6. Notify stakeholders with templated message and state expected rollback time.

Evidence Packet template (must be attached to any decision)
- Alert summary (ID, rule, start time)
- Affected tenants / API keys (top 10 by request rate)
- Recent deploys or config changes in last 24h
- Telemetry snapshot: latency P50/P95/P99; error-rate; CPU/GPU utilization; queue length; kernel OOMs
- Traffic shape: tokens-per-minute distribution, burstiness metric (CV of RPS)
- Headroom estimate: free GPUs, pre-warm pool size, cold-start time in seconds
- Proposed mitigation and rollback criteria

CLI & dashboard recipes (quick commands)
- Headroom summary (CLI): redwoodctl capacity headroom --service inference-api --window 5m --format table
Example output to paste in ticket: AvailableGPUs: 8; PrewarmSlots: 12; AvgColdStart: 28s
- Latency snapshot: redwoodctl telemetry snapshot --service inference-api --quantiles p50,p95,p99 --since 15m
- Tenant breakdown: redwoodctl telemetry tenant-top --metric rps --n 10
- Short synthetic canary (non-destructive): redwoodctl canary run --profile slo-regression --duration 3m --dry-run=false --target cluster-canary

Mitigation patterns (how to choose)
1) Soft-throttle + backpressure (preferred): apply per-tenant token rate limit to spread remaining capacity. Use when many tenants cause queueing but no single tenant dominates.
2) Priority lanes (token-priority): route critical customers to reserved lanes; move lower-tier tenants to degraded models/quantized variants.
3) Regional failover: shift traffic to secondary region if locality SLOs and data residency permit.
4) Canary reversion: if a recent model or infra change correlates with SLO drift, roll back the change and re-evaluate within 15 minutes.
5) Temporary burst-reserve: if expected spike is short (<30 minutes) and budget allows, provision burst GPUs with automatic scale-down policy.
6) Controlled eviction: soft-evict long-running batch jobs or non-critical precomputations to free GPU memory.

Execution playbook (step-by-step example: soft-throttle)
1. Run Evidence Packet template and attach to incident ticket.
2. Execute scaled throttle: redwoodctl throttle apply --service inference-api --policy soft --percent 20 --tenants low-tier
3. Monitor latency and errors at 1-minute cadence for 10 minutes.
4. If P99 latency improves by >=20% and error-rate <= target, continue and open a capacity-ticket for medium term.
5. If no improvement or user-visible errors increase, revert throttle and escalate to oncall lead.

Negotiating error-budget with Product and Sales (template conversation)
- Context: "We are currently burning 2.8% of the monthly availability error budget for inference-api vs 0.6% baseline. Headroom is limited; if burn continues we'll exceed the budget in ~36 hours."
- Ask: "Request temporary privilege to degrade low-tier model fidelity for 12 hours and provision 4 burst GPUs for immediate relief. We will revert when burn-rate normalizes or after 12 hours."
- Approval matrix: Tier-1 (oncall lead + product manager) approval for up to 12 hours and <= 8 GPU burst. Tier-2 (SRE director + sales lead) required if >12 hours or changes affecting billing/commit terms.

Operational tooling policies (what the steward must configure)
- Error-budget windows: default 28-day rolling window for availability, 7-day for latency-sensitive features.
- Auto-throttle thresholds: configure soft throttle when P95 latency > target by 50% and error-budget burn-rate over 2x baseline.
- Canary gating: every model rollout must pass the synthetic canary for 10m with p99 latency within 1.5x baseline before full deployment.

Incident review inputs (required for postmortem)
- Complete Evidence Packet at decision time (attach CLI outputs)
- Decision log: who approved mitigation, time, rollback criteria, and actual rollback time
- Telemetry traces (sampled): 10 full traces around incident peak and 100 token-level traces for latency distribution analysis
- Customer-impact log: list of customers notified, message copy sent, and any credits or escalations
- Follow-ups & action owners: capacity provisioning, autoscale tuning, alert refinement, and pre-warm policy changes

Playbook snippets (templates to copy)
1) Stakeholder notification (short):
Subject: [SLO] inference-api p95 elevated — mitigation in place
Body: We observed sustained p95 latency of 1.8s (target 0.9s) starting 2026-02-15T14:03Z. Oncall applied soft-throttle to low-tier tenants at 14:12Z. Expected reduction in 10–20min. We will update at 14:30Z or sooner.

2) Post-decision rollback note:
Action: soft-throttle removal
Reason: p95 improved to 0.85s and error-rate normalized
Time: 2026-02-15T14:34Z
Performed by: Ravi Kapoor

Capacity forecast worksheet (table — paste into ticket)
Columns: horizon|projected RPS|projected tokens/min|available GPUs|expected headroom GPUs|warm-pool slots|recommended action
Row example: 5m|12k|2.4M|48|4|16|soft-throttle low-tier

Metrics & SLO definitions (reference)
- availability: percent of requests completing with 2xx within 10s window; SLO 99.9% monthly
- latency: p95 request latency for standard generation; SLO 900ms rolling 7d
- correctness/error-rate: user-facing incorrect completions (model exceptions or 5xx) <0.1% weekly

Handoff & documentation standards
- All temporary mitigations must be recorded in the incident ticket with expected rollback time.
- If mitigation extends beyond 2 hours, assign an owner and schedule a stakeholder sync.
- Add capacity forecast table to the incident postmortem and tag related runbook pages.

Runbooks to review (recommended reading)
- capacity-onboarding-checklist-for-new-model-tenants-2026
- quantized-serving-slo-cost-tradeoff-runbook-2026
- cross-region-surge-and-emergency-slo-throttle-playbook-2026

Appendix A — Example alert rules (YAML)
- name: inference-api-p95-sustained
  expr: avg_over_time(latency_p95{service="inference-api"}[10m]) > 0.9
  for: 10m
  labels: {severity:"page"}
  annotations: {summary: "Sustained p95 above 900ms"}

Appendix B — Quick references for common CLI outputs (copy into ticket)
- redwoodctl capacity headroom ... -> paste AvailableGPUs/PrewarmSlots/AvgColdStart
- redwoodctl telemetry snapshot ... -> paste p50/p95/p99 lines and tenant top list

Appendix C — Decision examples from history
- 2025-11-03: Soft-throttle low-tier reduced p99 tail by 35% with zero customer credits required.
- 2026-01-12: Canary rollback prevented a mass p99 spike after a model quantization pipeline change.

Document change log
- 2026-02-15: Created initial field kit (Ravi Kapoor)
- 2026-03-02: Added CLI recipes and negotiation matrix (Emily Chen)

Related resources
- Link to capacity dashboard, canary runner, and incident template in internal tooling (see related_pages)

Feedback & maintenance
If you find gaps or repeated decisions not covered here, raise a PR to this page and tag the oncall rotation list. The document is reviewed quarterly or after any major SLO incident.
